lessons.title: Your dev environment
lessons.description: Build a working setup the way it really stacks up: system, package managers, runtimes, then each project with its own box of libraries. Then install it in the wrong order and watch it fail.

lessons.title: Git: save every version
lessons.description: Watch your changes travel from the working folder to the staging tray, get sealed into commits, branch off for an experiment and merge back. Then commit a 2 GB model file and force-push over a teammate.

lessons.title: GPUs: why AI needs graphics cards
lessons.description: Fill the same grid of sums with a CPU's eight strong cores and a graphics card's hundreds of small ones. Then check whether a model fits in the card's memory, and what a bigger card costs by the hour.

lessons.title: APIs and keys
lessons.description: Send a question down the road to a model service and watch the parcel come back with an answer and a bill. Then use a wrong key, send ten at once, and leak your key in public code.

lessons.title: Notebooks and the kernel
lessons.description: Run cells one by one and watch the kernel remember every variable, with answers and charts right beside the code. Then run them out of order and let hidden state lie to you.

lessons.title: Python environments and lock files
lessons.description: Watch a resolver walk the shelves of package versions and pick one of each that fits every rule, then write them into a lock file so Lagos and Kigali install exactly the same set. Then forget the lock file.

lessons.title: Docker: the same box everywhere
lessons.description: Build an image layer by layer, watch the cache skip what hasn't changed, then run it as a container that borrows the GPU and a folder of models, and ship the very same box to Accra, Nairobi and the cloud.

lessons.title: An editor that helps
lessons.description: Set up the three helpers every AI engineer leans on: a type checker that spots mistakes before you run, a formatter on save, and auto-save. Then reach a GPU box in Johannesburg from the same editor.

lessons.title: Data: splits, formats and streaming
lessons.description: Send fifty rows of farm records through a shuffle drum into train, validation and a locked test bin. Fix the seed and the split repeats exactly; forget it and your test set changes every run. Then compare CSV with Parquet, and stream instead of downloading 800 GB.

lessons.title: The terminal: pipes and sessions
lessons.description: Pour a training log through a pipeline of small commands until one number comes out: the best loss. Then keep training alive on a faraway server when your laptop closes, and see what > and 2>&1 really do.

lessons.title: Linux: files, permissions and disks
lessons.description: Walk the Linux file tree from / down to your project, flip the nine permission switches on a script, and watch checkpoints fill a 500 GB disk until training dies with "No space left on device".

lessons.title: Debugging a training loop
lessons.description: Send a batch round the five stations of a training step while a profiler times each one and a breakpoint stops it to look inside. Then make the loss turn NaN, feed the model the wrong shape, and starve the GPU of data.

lessons.title: Python for AI: lists, arrays and traps
lessons.description: See why a Python list of numbers is a row of pointers and a NumPy array is one solid block, and race them on a sum. Then fall into the three silent traps: rows that share one list, and a generator that is empty the second time.

lessons.title: Span, rank and projection
lessons.description: Mix two arrows to reach a point, and see that everything you can reach lies on one flat sheet: their span. Drop a target that sits off the sheet onto its nearest point (a projection), then add a third arrow that adds a new direction, or adds nothing at all.

lessons.title: Vectors: how alike are two things?
lessons.description: Turn jollof, suya, nyama choma and makroud into arrows. The angle between two arrows tells you how alike they are: the idea behind search, recommendations and every language model.

lessons.title: Matrices move space
lessons.description: Pick a 2 × 2 matrix and watch it rotate, stretch, shear or mirror a whole grid at once. The two arrows land on its columns, the determinant is how much area grows, and a few arrows only stretch: the eigenvectors.

lessons.title: Derivatives: the slope that teaches
lessons.description: Put a ball on a loss curve and draw the line that just touches it: its slope is the derivative. Estimate it by nudging the weight a little, then nudge too much, too little, and onto a kink.

lessons.title: The chain rule and autodiff
lessons.description: Draw a tiny model as a graph of simple steps. Push values forward, then send gradients backward, each step multiplying by its own slope: that is the chain rule, and it is all autodiff does. Then forget to zero the gradients.

lessons.title: Probability: the shape of chance
lessons.description: Drop balls through rows of pegs, where every bounce is a coin flip, and watch the bins fill into a bell curve. Then judge the shape from ten balls, and tilt the pegs.

lessons.title: Bayes: how sure after the alarm?
lessons.description: A fraud alarm on 1,000 mobile-money transfers catches 95% of frauds and wrongly flags 3% of honest ones. When it goes off, how likely is fraud? Count the flagged transfers and see why the answer is far below 95%, then check again.

lessons.title: Gradient descent
lessons.description: Roll a ball down a hill of mistakes. See how a model learns by taking small steps downhill, and what happens when the steps are too big.

lessons.title: Surprise, entropy and the loss
lessons.description: Forecast tomorrow's weather in Accra and measure how surprised the forecast is when the day comes. Average surprise is entropy; the forecast's average surprise is cross-entropy, the loss nearly every model learns from. Then give storms a 0% chance.

lessons.title: PCA: squash the data, keep the shape
lessons.description: A cloud of farms measured three ways floats in space. PCA finds the directions it spreads most, then flattens it onto the best sheet or line while keeping most of its shape. Then forget to centre the data, or measure one feature in bigger units.

lessons.title: SVD: a picture in layers
lessons.description: Split a woven pattern into layers, each a column pattern times a row pattern, sorted by strength. Rebuild it from the strongest few and keep most of the picture for a fraction of the numbers. Then try it on noise and on diagonal stripes.

lessons.title: Tensors: shapes, reshape and broadcasting
lessons.description: Hold a batch of four tiny images as a block of 48 numbered cubes and watch the same numbers sit in a single line of memory. Reshape, transpose and broadcast them, then make the shapes disagree.

lessons.title: Numbers that overflow
lessons.description: Softmax turns a model's scores into chances by raising e to each score. Push the scores up and the columns burst through the ceiling of what a float can hold: infinity, then NaN. Subtract the largest score first and every column fits.

lessons.title: Norms: three ways to measure distance
lessons.description: From the depot to the kiosk: straight as the crow flies, block by block along the streets, or just the longer leg. Watch the ring of "distance 1" become a circle, a diamond or a square, and see which shop is nearest by each measure.

lessons.title: Statistics: is it really better?
lessons.description: Model B scored 83% and model A 80% on the test set. Is B really better, or was it luck? Resample the test set 400 times and watch the pile of differences tell you how sure to be. Then test on 50 examples, try 20 models, and test on a million.

lessons.title: Sampling: drawing from any shape
lessons.description: A computer can only make flat random numbers, yet models need samples from every kind of shape. Throw darts and keep the ones under the curve, read across a running total, or send a walker uphill, and watch the bars fill into the right shape. Then waste darts, freeze the walker, and make it refuse every step.

lessons.title: Linear systems: two receipts, two prices
lessons.description: Two market receipts, two unknown prices. Each receipt becomes a line of prices that fit it, and where the lines cross is the answer. Eliminate to solve it, then try receipts that repeat themselves, nearly repeat, or disagree.

lessons.title: Convex problems: one bottom, guaranteed
lessons.description: Drop eight balls into a bowl and every one rolls to the same bottom; stretch a string between two points and it never dips under the surface. Then add a fence the answer must respect, make the ground bumpy, and ignore the fence.

lessons.title: Complex numbers: arrows that turn
lessons.description: A complex number is an arrow on a plane, and multiplying by one turns and stretches it. Multiply again and again and the tip walks round a circle, or spirals away, or spirals in. The same turning drives the Fourier transform and the position code inside transformers.

lessons.title: Fourier: splitting a sound into notes
lessons.description: Three kora strings sound together and make one wobbly wave. The Fourier transform splits it back into three clean bars, one per note. Then sample too slowly and watch a high note pretend to be a low one, or cut the high notes from a square wave and watch it ring.

lessons.title: Graphs: towns, roads and hops
lessons.description: Nine East African towns and the roads between them make a graph. Search outwards from Kampala ring by ring to find the fewest-hop route to Mombasa, see the same roads as a grid of 0s and 1s, then let floods close two roads and make the roads into Mombasa one-way.

lessons.title: Markov chains: tomorrow from today
lessons.description: Sun, cloud and rain are three stops, and arrows between them say how likely tomorrow's weather is given today's. Send a walker hopping day by day and watch the share of sunny days settle to the same mix, wherever it starts. Then trap it in the rain.

lessons.title: What is machine learning?
lessons.description: Sort mangoes into ripe and not yet ripe from their colour and softness. Write a rule by hand, flip a coin, or let a rule learn itself from labelled examples, then watch new mangoes get sorted. Then swap some labels and bring in a variety that stays green when ripe.

lessons.title: Linear regression
lessons.description: Guess a motorbike-taxi fare from the distance. Fit a straight line by hand, watch every miss as a square, then let the computer fit it for you.

lessons.title: Logistic regression: the chance of rain
lessons.description: Sixty days in Kampala: today's humidity, and whether it rained tomorrow. Fit an S-shaped curve that turns humidity into a chance of rain, pick a threshold, and count the hits, false alarms and misses. Then fit a straight line instead, and set the threshold far too low.

lessons.title: Decision trees: twenty questions for data
lessons.description: Which crop does best on a farm: tea, maize or sorghum? A decision tree asks one question at a time about rainfall and altitude, cutting the field into boxes. Grow it deeper and watch it fit the farms it learned from, then start memorising noise.

lessons.title: Support vector machines: the widest road
lessons.description: Draw the widest road you can between two groups of points: that is what a support vector machine does, and only the few points touching the road decide where it goes. Then add one mislabelled point, and a ring that no straight road can split until you lift it into a bowl.

lessons.title: Nearest neighbours: ask the ones most like you
lessons.description: A café in Kigali knows what its regulars drink and how they spend. When a new customer walks in, ask the most similar regulars and go with the majority. Change how many you ask, ask just one, ask everyone, then measure one thing in shillings and the other in days.

lessons.title: Clustering: groups with no labels
lessons.description: Ninety-six shops on a city map and nobody has said which belong together. Drop a few delivery depots, give each shop to its nearest depot, move each depot to the middle of its shops, and repeat until the zones settle. Then start badly, ask for too many zones, and stretch the map.

lessons.title: Feature engineering: better columns, better model
lessons.description: Predict how long a boda boda or okada trip takes from the hour, the distance, the city and the rain. Turn raw columns into useful features and watch the predictions line up with what really happened. Then number the cities 1, 2, 3, and slip in a column that leaks the answer.

lessons.title: Model evaluation: how good is it really?
lessons.description: A screener ranks microloan applicants by how likely they are to fall behind. Cut the data into five slices and let each take a turn as the test, then trace the ROC curve. Then tune on the test set until it lies to you, and report accuracy when almost nobody defaults.

lessons.title: Bias and variance: too stiff, too floppy
lessons.description: Maize yield rises with fertiliser, then levels off. Fit curves of different flexibility to ten different fields at once: stiff curves all miss the same way, floppy ones each chase their own noise. Find the sweet spot where new data is predicted best.

lessons.title: Ensembles: a forest beats a tree
lessons.description: One deep decision tree is jumpy: change a few farms and its answer changes. Grow many small trees, each on its own random sample of the farms, and let them vote. Watch nine trees disagree and the forest's vote come out smooth and steady. Then make every tree the same.

lessons.title: Tuning: searching for the best settings
lessons.description: The learning rate and the tree depth are settings you choose before training. Their best values hide on a narrow ridge. Search with a neat grid, scatter random tries, or zoom in near the best, and see which finds the ridge with the same nine tries. Then search the learning rate in plain steps.

lessons.title: Pipelines: the same steps, every time
lessons.description: Loan applications ride a conveyor through three stations: fill, scale, score. Training learns each station's settings once; live rows must replay them.

lessons.title: Naive Bayes: a spam filter from word counts
lessons.description: Each word in a text message is a small weight on a balance: "prize" and "claim" tip it towards spam, "market" and "mama" tip it back. Naive Bayes adds up every word's evidence on top of how common spam is. Then meet a word the filter has never seen in spam, and a message so long the numbers vanish.

lessons.title: Time series: forecasting tomorrow
lessons.description: Twelve weeks of milk deliveries to a dairy in Nakuru, rising slowly with a Saturday peak every week. Build a forecast from its parts, the trend, the weekly rhythm and yesterday, and test it on the two weeks held back. Then shuffle the days before testing, and forget the weekly rhythm.

lessons.title: Anomaly detection: spotting the odd one out
lessons.description: Two weeks of power use on a village solar mini-grid in Tanzania, with an evening peak every day. Flag readings that sit too far from normal: a sudden spike, a dead hour, and a surge at 2 in the morning that is only strange for its time. Then let one giant spike hide the rest.

lessons.title: Imbalanced data: when the rare case matters
lessons.description: Of 500 cassava leaves, only 25 have mosaic disease. A plain classifier can be 95% accurate by calling every leaf healthy, and miss every sick one. Weigh the rare class more, or show it more often, and watch the boundary move to catch the disease.

lessons.title: Feature selection: fewer, better columns
lessons.description: Predict a school's pass rate from twelve columns: teachers per pupil, textbooks and electricity matter; the gate's colour and the head teacher's shoe size don't. With only 40 schools to learn from, every useless column makes predictions worse. Find the ones worth keeping, then keep a copy of a column, and choose columns using the test set.

lessons.title: ML system design: from a goal to a running system
lessons.description: A pharmacy chain wants fewer empty shelves. Design the whole system, not just the model: what to predict, who acts on it, how often to run it, what it costs, which numbers to watch, and how to roll it out safely. Then build a prediction nobody uses, score live around the clock, and let the model starve its own data.

lessons.title: Monitoring: when the world moves on
lessons.description: A crop-loan model learned from last season's farmers. Week after week new applicants arrive. Watch their rainfall shift away from what the model knew, catch it with a drift score long before repayments reveal the damage, and see why a change in who repays is harder to spot.

lessons.title: Feature stores: one recipe for training and serving
lessons.description: A mobile-money fraud model uses "transfers in the last hour". Training computes it one way from old logs, the live app another way from the stream, and the two quietly disagree. Put one feature store between them, then let the training join peek at the future, and let the cache go stale.

lessons.title: The perceptron
lessons.description: Teach one artificial neuron to tell which plantains are ready for dodo. Watch its fence move with every mistake, then give it a puzzle it can never solve.

lessons.title: Layers: neurons working together
lessons.description: Good phone signal sits in a patch around the mast, and no single straight fence can enclose a patch. Give the network a hidden layer: each hidden neuron draws its own fence, and the output neuron combines them into a closed shape. Then take away the activation, keep just one neuron, and start every weight the same.

lessons.title: Backpropagation
lessons.description: Watch a small neural network learn. Answers flow forward in gold, the blame flows back in red, and every wire changes a little. This is how all neural networks learn.

lessons.title: Activation functions
lessons.description: The small bend inside every neuron. Slide along ReLU, sigmoid and GELU, then watch a tiny network bend a line into the shape of Lagos rainfall. Take the bend away and it can only draw a straight line.

lessons.title: Loss functions: how wrong is wrong?
lessons.description: Training lowers one number, the loss, so how you score mistakes decides what the model learns. Squared error hates big misses, absolute error treats them evenly, Huber does both, and cross-entropy punishes a confident wrong chance without limit. Then add one typo to the data and watch squared error chase it.

lessons.title: Optimizers: smarter steps downhill
lessons.description: Three balls race down a long, narrow valley. Plain gradient descent zigzags from wall to wall, momentum builds speed along the floor, and Adam gives each direction its own step size. Then turn the step up until plain descent bounces out, and take away momentum's friction.

lessons.title: Regularization: stop memorising, start learning
lessons.description: A small network learns maize harvest from rainfall on twelve Rift Valley farms. Train too long and it memorises each farm's luck; decay, dropout and stopping calm it.

lessons.title: Weight initialization: starting the signal right
lessons.description: A signal travels through 24 layers, each a glass pane with sixteen neurons inside. Start the weights at the right size and the signal arrives intact. Start them too small and it fades to nothing; too big and it explodes. Make every weight the same and all the neurons turn into copies.

lessons.title: Learning rate schedules: fast, then careful
lessons.description: Training runs left to right along a valley that starts narrow and widens. The back wall shows the learning rate at every step against a red safe limit. Warm up gently, go fast in the middle, then slow down to settle at the bottom. Skip the warmup and it blows up; never slow down and it jitters forever.

lessons.title: A mini framework: the parts of PyTorch
lessons.description: The parts of deep learning on one assembly line: a loader, a row of modules, a loss and an optimizer. Forget zero_grad, step or the activations, and see what stops.

lessons.title: PyTorch: tensors, autograd and devices
lessons.description: Watch a PyTorch training step for boda-boda trip times in Kampala. Tensors sit on a device, every operation adds a node to the autograd graph as it runs, and backward() fills each weight's gradient. Then leave the data on the CPU, switch off requires_grad, or forget torch.no_grad() and watch memory climb.

lessons.title: JAX: grad, jit, vmap and random keys
lessons.description: A pure function rides through three stations: grad, jit, vmap. Random numbers come from keys you split by hand; reuse one, or change the shape, and watch the clock.

lessons.title: Debugging neural networks: tests before training
lessons.description: A small network should predict cattle prices in Mombasa, and it will not learn. Work through the checks in order: one batch, the learning rate, then the gradients.

lessons.title: Images as numbers: pixels and channels
lessons.description: A baobab at sunset, built from 384 pixel tiles, and beside it the same picture split into red, green and blue columns. Every colour is three numbers. Then read the channels in the wrong order, cut the bits until the sky bands, and squash the picture by resizing it carelessly.

lessons.title: Convolutions
lessons.description: Slide a 3×3 window over an adire pattern built from pillars. Each stop multiplies nine numbers and adds them up. Edges, blur and sharpening fall out of that one move, and it is how computers see.

lessons.title: CNNs: from LeNet to ResNet
lessons.description: A cassava leaf goes in on the left and passes through a row of feature maps that shrink and thicken layer by layer. The square on the leaf shows how much one final neuron can see. Stack more layers, add pooling, then take away ResNet's skip connections and watch the gradient fade.

lessons.title: Image classification: sorting maize leaves
lessons.description: Photo cards of maize leaves leave a hopper one at a time, the classifier shows three confidence bars, and each card drops into a bin. Then read the confusion.

lessons.title: Transfer learning: borrow what a model knows
lessons.description: A tower of layers already trained on a million everyday photos gets a new head for three cattle breeds: Ankole, Boran and Friesian, from just 40 photos. Lock the lower layers, unlock the top ones, and compare with starting from nothing. Then unfreeze everything with a big learning rate and watch it forget.

lessons.title: Object detection: boxes, confidence and NMS
lessons.description: A Lagos street on a 7 × 7 grid: every cell guesses boxes for danfo buses, okadas and people. A confidence threshold drops weak guesses and non-max suppression keeps the best of each overlapping pile. Then switch NMS off, set the threshold too high, or squeeze the overlap limit until a person vanishes from beside their friend.

lessons.title: Segmentation: a label for every pixel
lessons.description: A satellite tile on the shore of Lake Victoria, labelled pixel by pixel as lake, field, road or roof by a U-Net. The encoder shrinks the picture to understand it, the decoder grows it back, and skip connections carry the fine detail across. Remove them, make the U shallow, or forget class weighting and watch the roads vanish.

lessons.title: Instance segmentation: which goat is which
lessons.description: Goats crowded together at a market in Kano. Semantic segmentation paints them all one colour; instance segmentation gives each its own mask, so you can count them and tell where one ends and the next begins. Then swap RoIAlign for RoIPool and watch every mask slide, shrink the masks to blobs, or cut the proposals.

lessons.title: GANs: weaving pictures from noise
lessons.description: A GAN generator turns a handful of random numbers into a cloth swatch, growing it layer by layer from 4 × 4 to full size. Nine noise vectors give nine different swatches, and walking through the noise morphs them smoothly. Then watch it collapse to one design, fill with a checkerboard, or never learn at all.

lessons.title: Diffusion: pictures out of noise
lessons.description: Noise is added to a picture step by step, and a network learns to take it back out. Run it the other way, from pure static, and a picture forms.

lessons.title: Stable Diffusion: the parts and a fine-tune
lessons.description: Stable Diffusion works small: a prompt steers denoising in a tiny latent, and a decoder paints the full picture. Turn the guidance up, and see what it costs.

lessons.title: Video: when order matters
lessons.description: A clip of a market stall holds its story in time. Sample frames, stack them, and compare a 2D model that sees pictures with one that sees motion.

lessons.title: NeRF: a scene stored as a function
lessons.description: A round thatched hut in the Lesotho highlands, a camera, and rays fired through every pixel. A NeRF stores the whole scene as a function from a point to a density and a colour; each pixel marches along its ray, sampling as it goes, and adds up what it meets. Then take too few samples, drop the positional encoding, or nudge the camera poses and watch the picture fail.

lessons.title: Vision transformers: a picture as tokens
lessons.description: A zebra at a waterhole in Etosha, cut into square patches. Each patch becomes a token with a position, and a transformer lets every patch look at every other before a special [CLS] token gives the answer. Then try patches that are too big or too small, take away the positions and shuffle the picture, or train from scratch on too little data.

lessons.title: Edge vision: fast enough, small enough
lessons.description: A camera on a Lagos toll gate must count cars on a small chip, in real time. Trade size for speed: quantise, prune, and watch the frame budget.

lessons.title: A full vision pipeline, end to end
lessons.description: Capstone: a farm-photo service runs intake, model, checks and a cheap fallback from end to end. Each stage has a job, and each failure a place to be caught.

lessons.title: Self-supervised vision: learning without labels
lessons.description: Sixty unlabelled photos from a market in Addis Ababa, each seen twice through random crops and colour changes.

lessons.title: CLIP: matching pictures and words
lessons.description: Search photos for a label no model was trained on. CLIP scores each picture against each phrase, so write the classes as sentences and read the grid.

lessons.title: OCR: reading text in photos
lessons.description: A clinic scans handwritten forms. Find the text, read each line with CTC, and keep the layout, or the right words land in the wrong boxes.

lessons.title: Image retrieval: find this fabric
lessons.description: A shop in Lagos lets customers snap a photo of an Ankara print and finds it in a catalogue of 40. The catalogue is ranked by distance in a learned embedding space and the best five rise on stands. Train with triplets, then set the margin to zero, mine only easy negatives, or compare raw vector lengths and watch the wrong prints win.

lessons.title: Pose: finding joints with heatmaps
lessons.description: A runner training at altitude in Iten, Kenya. The network draws one glowing heatmap per joint, the brightest spot becomes the joint, and the joints join into a skeleton that gives the coach a knee angle. Then shrink the heatmaps until joints snap to a grid, flip training photos without swapping left and right, or let two runners' boxes overlap.

lessons.title: Gaussian splatting: a scene made of soft blobs
lessons.description: A clay water pot from a potter in Kwali, Nigeria, stored as hundreds of soft coloured blobs. To draw any view, every blob is projected as a soft ellipse, sorted front to back and blended by opacity, fast enough for real time. Turn the camera, then skip densification, forget the depth sort, or make every blob opaque.

lessons.title: Rectified flow: straight paths from noise
lessons.description: Every generated picture shrunk to a dot on a table, so you can watch its whole journey from noise on the left to real cloth on the right: indigo adire or gold kente. A transformer predicts the velocity at each step; straighten the paths and one or two steps are enough. Then take two steps on curved paths, hide the timestep, or push the guidance too far.

lessons.title: Segment anything you can name
lessons.description: A fish stall on the shore of Lake Malawi. Type a short phrase and the model masks every match; click one fish and it masks just that one.

lessons.title: Vision-language models: a picture becomes words
lessons.description: A photo is cut into patches, made to look like words, and read by a language model with the question. See where it reads and where it guesses.

lessons.title: Depth from a single photo
lessons.description: One photo of a roadside near Musanze, Rwanda: a shop, a banana tree, a house and terraced hills. A depth network turns it into a depth map, and with the camera's focal length every pixel lifts into a 3D point on the bench. Then read relative depth as metres, point it at a shop window, or give it the wrong focal length.

lessons.title: Tracking: keeping every ID
lessons.description: Four boda-boda motorbikes cross a junction in Kampala, seen from above. A detector finds them in every frame, and the tracker predicts where each should be, matches predictions to detections and keeps their IDs, even behind a parked lorry. Then match in arrival order, switch off prediction, or throw away the unsure detections and count the ID switches.

lessons.title: World models: imagining what happens next
lessons.description: A video model imagines frames forward from a scene. Give it actions, and see the prediction drift from the truth the further it looks.

lessons.title: Generative models: five families
lessons.description: Five families of generative model, one job: make something new. Compare how each learns the data, what it pays in speed and quality, and where it fell over.

lessons.title: Autoencoders and VAEs: squeeze, then rebuild
lessons.description: Chalk symbols drawn by children at a school in Lusaka are squeezed into just two numbers and rebuilt. Every drawing lands as a dot in the code space, and a probe wanders across it while the decoder draws what lives there. A plain autoencoder leaves gaps full of nonsense; a VAE packs the codes into one smooth cloud. Then set the KL weight to zero or far too high, or sample far outside the cloud.

lessons.title: GANs: the forger and the inspector
lessons.description: A real, tiny GAN trains here on mango weights from a market in Mombasa: small Ngowe and large Apple mangoes, two humps. The generator's fake weights (orange) chase the real ones (teal) while the discriminator's curve (purple) tries to tell them apart. Then use the saturating loss, a lazy discriminator, or a generator with one neuron.

lessons.title: Pix2pix: from sketch to picture
lessons.description: An architect's line drawing of a Stone Town house front in Zanzibar goes in, and a rendered façade comes out, judged by a discriminator that sees the sketch too. Swap sketches to see the output follow its input. Then drop the L1 term, hide the sketch from the discriminator, or use L1 alone and compare the three boards.

lessons.title: StyleGAN: styles at every scale
lessons.description: A generator makes beaded collars in the style of Maasai beadwork, three at a time. A mapping network turns each random seed into a style that is fed into every layer: coarse layers choose the shape, middle layers the colour bands, fine layers the bead texture, and noise adds the tiny variations. Mix styles between collars, then remove the mapping network, set truncation to zero, or switch off the noise.

lessons.title: DDPM: the maths of noise and back
lessons.description: The maths behind diffusion, on a picture of a lilac-breasted roller over the Okavango Delta. The schedule says how much picture survives at every step, a single formula jumps straight to any step, and the reverse process walks back from noise. Then drop the square roots, squeeze a linear schedule into 200 steps, or leave out the sampling noise.

lessons.title: Latent diffusion: denoise a smaller picture
lessons.description: Why Stable Diffusion works in a compressed space. A hand-painted kiosk sign in Mombasa is squeezed by a VAE into a small grid of numbers, diffusion runs there, and the decoder expands it back. Slide the squeeze factor and watch the cost of every step fall while the lettering holds, until it does not. Then diffuse in pixel space, squeeze too hard, or forget the latent scaling factor.

lessons.title: ControlNet and LoRA: steering an image model
lessons.description: An illustrator wants a figure mid-jump, as in the Maasai adumu jumping dance, in a flat poster style. The prompt sets the subject, a ControlNet reads a pose skeleton to fix the layout, and a small LoRA adds the style. Compare with the prompt alone, then set the control strength to zero or far too high, or initialise the ControlNet the wrong way.

lessons.title: Inpainting and editing: changing part of a photo
lessons.description: A photo of a hillside street in Kigali with a delivery truck parked in the way. Mask the truck and the model fills the hole to match its surroundings; widen the canvas and it continues the street; or noise the photo part way and denoise it towards a new prompt. Then draw the mask too tight, paste the fill back without blending, or push the edit strength too far.

lessons.title: Video generation: frames that agree
lessons.description: An eight-frame clip of a dhow sailing across the harbour at Lamu, generated from a prompt. The track below plots where the boat is in each frame and the colour of its sail. Temporal layers keep the frames in agreement; generate each frame on its own, freeze them with one seed, or ask for four times the trained length and watch it fall apart.

lessons.title: Audio generation: sound as tokens
lessons.description: A two-second highlife guitar riff, turned by a neural codec into a grid of tokens, eight codebooks deep, then predicted by a language model and decoded back to sound. Watch the spectrogram fill in as codebooks are added. Then decode with one codebook, play at the wrong sample rate, or sample far too hot.

lessons.title: 3D generation: views that agree
lessons.description: "A carved wooden giraffe" becomes a 3D object. A multi-view diffusion model draws it from four angles at once so the views agree, then a reconstruction step fits a 3D shape to all four. Turn the carving on its turntable, then draw each view separately and get a two-headed giraffe, use a single view, or drop the camera angles.

lessons.title: Flow matching: learning straight lines
lessons.description: Flow matching as training sees it: noise on the left, data on the right (grain sizes of teff and wheat at an Ethiopian market), and a straight line from each noise sample to a data sample. The network learns the average slope through every point. Random pairs cross and curve; reflowed pairs run straight, so one step lands. Then set the target backwards, or train only on early times.

lessons.title: Evaluating generators: FID, CLIP and people
lessons.description: One number cannot judge pictures. FID compares crowds of pictures to real ones, CLIP checks the prompt, and each is fooled by something different.

lessons.title: VAR: predicting the next scale
lessons.description: A painted Ndebele house wall built coarse to fine: one colour, then 2 × 2, 4 × 4, 8 × 8 and 16 × 16, each scale predicted all at once and adding detail on top of the last. Five steps instead of 256. Then switch to one token at a time in reading order, skip the middle scales, or drop the residual.

lessons.title: Tokens
lessons.description: Watch a tokenizer chop sentences into pieces on a conveyor. The same greeting costs far more tokens in Yoruba than in English. See why, and type your own.

lessons.title: Text processing: from messages to words
lessons.description: Customer messages to a Nairobi bus company ride down a line of five stations. Each one throws something away, so watch what the counts lose, and what they should not.

lessons.title: Bag of words and TF-IDF
lessons.description: Six notices on a market board in Kampala become a block of numbers: a row each, a column per word. Weigh words by rarity, and see what the grid cannot tell.

lessons.title: Word embeddings
lessons.description: Fly through a space where every word is a point. Countries, capitals and dishes line up so neatly that Abuja − Nigeria + Kenya lands on Nairobi.

lessons.title: GloVe and FastText: vectors for words
lessons.description: Swahili words from a school in Mombasa, each placed on a map by its meaning. An unseen word has no place in GloVe, but FastText can build one from its pieces.

lessons.title: Sentiment analysis: happy or not
lessons.description: A Naive Bayes classifier trains on 28 reviews of a waakye spot in Accra and learns a weight for every word: green for happy, red for unhappy. Test reviews ride to a scale and are sorted. Then switch off negation handling and watch "not good" come out happy, drop smoothing, or train on mostly happy reviews and see why accuracy alone lies.

lessons.title: Named entities: people, places, companies
lessons.description: A news line about a trip from Nairobi to Malindi, tagged word by word. Flags mark the names found; swap the tagger and see which it misses or runs together.

lessons.title: Parts of speech and parsing
lessons.description: "Fishermen in Mwanza fish at night." Each word gets a part-of-speech cap, and a dependency parse draws arches from each word to the word it depends on.

lessons.title: CNNs and RNNs for text
lessons.description: Two reviews of a bus from Nairobi to Kisumu, read three ways. A CNN slides a window of a few words and keeps the strongest match; an RNN reads word by word, carrying a memory; an LSTM adds gates so that memory lasts. Bars show how much of the first word each model still remembers. Then shrink the window to one word, read the long review with a plain RNN, or leave the padding unmasked.

lessons.title: Sequence to sequence: encode, then decode
lessons.description: An encoder reads an English sentence about a market by Lake Victoria and squeezes it into one context vector; a decoder writes the Swahili one word at a time, feeding each word back in. Then send a long sentence through that single vector, decode greedily and watch a word repeat, or train without teacher forcing and watch the loss stall.

lessons.title: Attention: look back at every word
lessons.description: Translating "the market near the lake opens early" into Swahili, the decoder looks back at every word for each word it writes. A field of towers shows where.

lessons.title: Machine translation: judging the output
lessons.description: A clinic in Dodoma translates its medicine labels into Swahili. Three systems, three kinds of mistake, and scores that cannot tell a paraphrase from a wrong dose.

lessons.title: Summarisation: the gist, and only the truth
lessons.description: A seven-sentence report from a county council meeting in Kisumu. Link the sentences, pick the central ones, and watch rewriting bring in a number no one said.

lessons.title: Question answering: find the words
lessons.description: A farming help line in Malawi answers questions from two leaflets. Each word is a tile, and the reader lifts a start and an end, or says there is no answer.

lessons.title: Search: keywords, meaning and both
lessons.description: The help centre of an invented solar-box seller searches its articles three ways. Keywords catch the code, meaning catches the words, and fusion needs both.

lessons.title: Topic modelling: what are people asking?
lessons.description: Sixteen text messages reach a farm radio show. LDA finds the topics on its own: each message a column of colours, each topic a stack of its top words.

lessons.title: N-grams: the next word from counts
lessons.description: A bigram model learns eight station announcements, from Kumasi to Mombasa, by counting pairs of words. A word pair it never saw has a chance of nothing, until you smooth.

lessons.title: Chatbots: rules, lookup and agents
lessons.description: A coach company's chat sends each message to the right machine: rules for risky acts, lookup for common questions, an agent for the rest. Then watch an injection.

lessons.title: Multilingual: one model, many languages
lessons.description: One sentiment model reads customer messages in English, Swahili, Hausa, Yoruba, Amharic and isiZulu. Teach it in one language, add a few Amharic examples, and read the score for each language. Then report only the average, push the learning rate too high, or use an English-only tokenizer.

lessons.title: Subwords: BPE, WordPiece, Unigram
lessons.description: Four tokenizers learn from Swahili verb forms like ninakula, "I am eating", and tutaenda, "we will go".

lessons.title: Structured outputs: decode to a schema
lessons.description: A hardware supplier in Kumasi turns customer messages into delivery records, while the schema masks every token it may not write.

lessons.title: Inference: does the text support it?
lessons.description: A summary of a Lusaka water notice is checked claim by claim: is each entailed, neutral or contradicted? The reader must read both sides, not just the claim.

lessons.title: Embeddings: how short can they be?
lessons.description: An archive in Accra searches eighty documents by embedding. A Matryoshka-trained model can be cut short and still find the right document; a plain one cannot. Then cut too far, cut the wrong kind of model, or query with a different model from the one that built the index.

lessons.title: Chunking: cut documents for RAG
lessons.description: A tenancy agreement for flats in Nairobi is cut into chunks four ways. Chunk too small and the answer splits; too big and it drowns. Add context, then the parent.

lessons.title: Coreference: who is "she"?
lessons.description: A short news item about a coffee cooperative in Huye, Rwanda, says "she", "it" and "he". Arcs link each mention back; one bad link joins two different people.

lessons.title: Entity linking: which Victoria?
lessons.description: Four mentions from African news are linked to a knowledge base: which Victoria, which Niger? Popularity alone picks wrong; the sentence around the name decides.

lessons.title: Relations: from text to a graph
lessons.description: A model reads four sentences about an invented solar company in Nakuru and writes a graph. Check every edge against the text, or it invents a place.

lessons.title: Evaluating LLMs: judge the judge
lessons.description: Twenty test questions for a farm advice bot are scored for faithfulness by people and by an LLM judge, and a release gate opens if the judge's average is high enough. Then use a judge that likes long answers, drop the judge's broken replies, or let the bot grade itself.

lessons.title: Long context: what really fits?
lessons.description: A court records office in Lagos wants to feed whole case files to a model that advertises 128,000 tokens. Test it across every length and every depth, and find the length it can really use. Then test only the ends, test only simple lookups, or plant a fact that shares words with the question.

lessons.title: Dialogue state: keep track of the booking
lessons.description: A customer books a coach from Dar es Salaam to Arusha in five short turns. Keep the whole state, not the last message, and let new answers overwrite old.

lessons.title: Audio: samples, Nyquist, Fourier
lessons.description: A field recorder in Kakamega Forest samples a sunbird's call. See the real wave, the samples taken from it, and the frequencies a Fourier transform finds in them. Then sample too slowly with no filter, turn the gain up until it clips, or use a tiny transform.

lessons.title: Spectrograms: sound as a landscape
lessons.description: One second of sound becomes a landscape: time runs across, pitch rises towards you, height is loudness. A talking drum glides upward, two slaps crack, a quiet whistle sings high. Then use plain loudness, a long window, or frequency rows in plain hertz.

lessons.title: Audio classes: what made that sound?
lessons.description: Listening posts in a forest reserve in Gabon label every sound: bird, elephant, vehicle, chainsaw or gunshot. A new clip takes the label of its nearest labelled neighbours.

lessons.title: Speech recognition: frames to words
lessons.description: A speech model hears "meet at Kejetia", the big market in Kumasi, as 28 short frames. Collapse the repeats, drop the blanks, and let beam search fix the rest.

lessons.title: Whisper: one model, many tasks
lessons.description: A radio station in Mombasa runs Swahili interviews through Whisper. Audio is cut into thirty-second trays, and a jingle or a wrong language tag gives you hallucinations.

lessons.title: Speaker verification: is it really you?
lessons.description: An invented mobile-money helpline in Uganda lets customers log in by voice. Genuine and impostor calls pile up by how closely they match the enrolled voiceprint, and a gate at the threshold decides. Then lower the threshold, take calls on a cheap phone line, or enrol from one noisy sample.

lessons.title: Text to speech: words into sound
lessons.description: The public-address system at an Accra bus station reads out "Bus to Nkawkaw at 2:30 pm". Normalise the numbers, teach it the local name, and match the sample rate.

lessons.title: Voice cloning: with consent only
lessons.description: An audiobook studio in Lagos voices a story in a narrator's voice. Three inputs reach a decoder, but only past a consent gate, and every output carries a mark.

lessons.title: Music generation: one token at a time
lessons.description: A small model writes highlife loops for a producer in Accra, one step at a time: bell, kick, shaker and bass. Turn the temperature up until the bell pattern falls apart, let it run past its memory until it loops, or ask for a living artist's style with the filter off.

lessons.title: Audio-language models: ask the recording
lessons.description: A call centre in Nairobi asks an audio-language model about recorded calls. The projector lands sound among word tokens; without it, frames fall outside.

lessons.title: Real-time audio: every millisecond counts
lessons.description: A voice line for a clinic in Kigali streams 20 ms audio frames through eight stages. Each one spends part of a budget, so stay under the line that feels instant.

lessons.title: Voice assistant: the whole pipeline
lessons.description: Farmers near Arusha phone a voice assistant for prices. Each part adds delay before the first word, and each one can fail.

lessons.title: Audio codecs: sound as tokens
lessons.description: A voice-note app on weak 2G networks in Ethiopia sends codec tokens instead of audio. Each codebook codes what the last one left over, a few numbers a frame.

lessons.title: Turn-taking: when has she finished?
lessons.description: A woman calls a microfinance helpline from a busy Kampala market and pauses to remember her account number. Frame by frame, a detector scores speech, and the system decides when her turn is over. Then use a plain loudness gate, a short hang-over, or no pre-roll.

lessons.title: Live translation: speak while listening
lessons.description: A cloth trader in Dakar speaks French and a buyer in Accra hears English, live. The model listens and speaks at once, with text inside.

lessons.title: Spotting fakes: watermarks and detectors
lessons.description: A fact-check desk in Johannesburg gets a viral voice note said to be a city official. Three checks stand in a row, and a re-encode can strip the hidden mark.

lessons.title: Audio evaluation: measure what matters
lessons.description: A team in Dar es Salaam tests a Swahili speech recogniser. Score a sentence word by word, then each group of speakers, not one average.

lessons.title: Why transformers? Look everywhere at once
lessons.description: To match "were" with "bales" across a long sentence, a model must carry it all the way. An RNN passes a baton word by word; a transformer lets each word look back.

lessons.title: Self-attention
lessons.description: Board a danfo (a matatu in Nairobi, a trotro in Accra) where every word is a passenger. Pick one and see who it looks at. Change one word at the end of the sentence and "it" switches from the bus to the park.

lessons.title: Multi-head attention
lessons.description: Four attention heads, stacked like glass shelves over one sentence. Each one hunts for a different pattern. Make them all the same and watch the model lose sight of who "she" is.

lessons.title: Positional encoding
lessons.description: "Lion chases goat" and "Goat chases lion" use the same words. Without positions a transformer can't tell them apart. Turn on the position dials and the difference appears.

lessons.title: The full transformer: encoder and decoder
lessons.description: An encoder-decoder transformer translates "Ninakwenda sokoni kununua nyanya" from Swahili into English. Watch the signal and the gradient through every layer, and the bridges between the towers. Then build a plain deep stack, leave out normalisation, or cut the cross-attention bridges.

lessons.title: BERT: fill in the blank
lessons.description: BERT learns by hiding words and guessing them from both sides of the gap. Watch the guesses change as the clues come and go.

lessons.title: T5 and BART: fix the broken sentence
lessons.description: Encoder-decoder models learn by repairing damaged text. T5 swaps spans for numbered sentinels and writes them back; BART rebuilds the whole sentence.

lessons.title: Vision transformers, inside
lessons.description: A team mapping smallholder fields in Mali runs a vision transformer over satellite tiles. See how image size and patch size set the number of tokens, what attention costs, and how patch tokens become a field map. Then run a big tile with global attention, use the [CLS] token alone, or forget to stretch the position embeddings.

lessons.title: Audio transformers: inside Whisper
lessons.description: A Kigali radio station captions its call-in show live with a Whisper-shaped model, re-reading the last 30 seconds every second. Follow 30 seconds of audio through the log-mel image, the convolutional stem, the encoder and the decoder, with the shape at every stage and the time it takes. Then feed in audio at the wrong sample rate, remove the stem, or use the full-depth decoder.

lessons.title: Mixture of experts: route each token
lessons.description: A helpdesk model in Kano reads Hausa, English, code and numbers. A router sends each token to a few of eight expert networks, so only a fraction of the model runs per token. Then switch off load balancing, cap each expert with only one choice per token, or send every token to all eight.

lessons.title: KV cache: memory for every word
lessons.description: A legal-research assistant at a firm in Lagos serves long contracts on one 80 GB GPU.

lessons.title: Scaling laws: spend compute wisely
lessons.description: A lab in Nairobi has a fixed compute budget to train a Swahili and English model.

lessons.title: Capstone: build a transformer
lessons.description: A class in Dar es Salaam builds a small character-level transformer on Swahili proverbs, part by part, then finds the learning rate that lets the loss fall.

lessons.title: Attention variants: who reads whom
lessons.description: A model reads a long Hausa news report, and the question at the end needs a name from the first line.

lessons.title: Speculative decoding: draft, then check
lessons.description: A Yoruba customer-support bot answers with a big model and a small draft model. The draft guesses ahead, the big one checks them all at once and keeps what fits.

lessons.title: Patch tokens: what the model sees
lessons.description: A travel assistant reads the departures board at a Lusaka bus terminus through a phone camera. The photo becomes patch tokens; their size, a few register tokens and the hand-off to the language model decide whether the times can be read. Then drop the registers, use patches bigger than the letters, or pool everything into one vector.

lessons.title: CLIP: match pictures to words
lessons.description: Eight photos from a Ghanaian picture library and their captions. Two encoders learn, live, to put each photo beside its own caption: the gold diagonal rises.

lessons.title: BLIP-2: a small bridge between giants
lessons.description: A camera-trap project in the Serengeti asks a frozen language model about bursts of frames from a frozen image encoder.

lessons.title: Flamingo: open the gate slowly
lessons.description: A gallery in Lagos writes catalogue labels from an interleaved prompt: two example images with labels, then a new image.

lessons.title: LLaVA: teach it to answer about images
lessons.description: A farm advice app in Kenya lets farmers photograph a maize leaf and ask what is wrong. A small projector carries image patches into a language model.

lessons.title: Any resolution: pack, don't squash
lessons.description: A land-records office in Kumasi sends one batch of three scans: a tall title deed, a wide survey map and a square ID photo. Fit them by squashing, padding, tiling or packing native patches into one sequence. Then squash everything square, pad everything square, or pack without the mask.

lessons.title: VLM recipes: what actually matters
lessons.description: A university team in Accra builds a vision-language model from open parts to read local documents and scenes.

lessons.title: OneVision: one model, three shapes
lessons.description: A road-safety team in Nairobi uses one model for a dashcam photo, four camera views of a junction and a 30-second clip. Each input gets a different shape within a similar token budget, and training goes single images first. Then feed video without pooling, sample only four frames, or train on video first.

lessons.title: Qwen-VL: real time in the tokens
lessons.description: A sports desk in Lagos logs the goals in a two-minute clip. Pick the frame rate and size, and see if the goal's time comes out right.

lessons.title: InternVL3: trained multimodal from the start
lessons.description: A public-health agency in Addis Ababa wants one model that writes clear reports and reads charts and clinic photos.

lessons.title: Chameleon: pictures as tokens
lessons.description: A children's-book studio in Kigali wants one model that writes a story and draws its pictures in the same reply.

lessons.title: Emu3: draw by predicting the next token
lessons.description: A textile shop in Dar es Salaam asks for "a kitenge print in blue and gold stripes". The model writes the picture one token at a time, like a sentence, and classifier-free guidance pulls it towards the caption. Then switch guidance off, turn the temperature up, or guide far too hard.

lessons.title: Transfusion: next token and diffusion together
lessons.description: A school-book publisher in Lusaka wants one model that writes a caption and paints the picture. One transformer predicts text token by token and denoises image patches, with a mask that is causal for text and two-way inside the image. Then make the image mask causal, use only four denoising steps, or squeeze patches into a codebook.

lessons.title: Show-o: unmask the picture
lessons.description: A craft cooperative in Bahir Dar previews new designs for woven basket lids. The picture starts fully masked; each step the model predicts every hidden code at once and keeps only the ones it is surest of. Then do it all in one step, keep codes at random, or use a model trained only with light masking.

lessons.title: Janus-Pro: two eyes, one brain
lessons.description: A tourism office in Marrakech uses one model to answer questions about visitors' photos and to make posters of the medina. Janus-Pro gives understanding and generation separate encoders and one shared transformer. Then use the generation tokenizer to understand, use the understanding encoder to generate, or shrink the model and its data.

lessons.title: MIO: hear, see, speak back
lessons.description: A farm helpline in Tamale: a farmer describes a sick maize plant aloud and sends a photo of the leaf, and one model listens, looks and answers out loud. MIO gives every modality its own range in one vocabulary and streams speech tokens out. Then let the ranges overlap, decode the speech levels one by one, or skip a training stage.

lessons.title: Video: when did it happen?
lessons.description: A conservancy near Etosha asks a video model when the lion charges in a five-minute clip. Choose how frames are sampled and how many tokens each one keeps.

lessons.title: Long video: hours, not minutes
lessons.description: A newsroom in Kisumu asks when a county council voted on the market-roof repair in a recording up to three hours long. Read it all in one long context spread over a ring of GPUs, squeeze it into summary tokens, or let an agent fetch the right clips. Then run three hours on one GPU, ask summary tokens for an exact moment, or give the agent a weak retriever.

lessons.title: Audio models: hear more than words
lessons.description: A radio archive in Dakar asks questions about old recordings: what an interview is about, which instrument leads, whether a crowd is cheering, who speaks last. Compare transcribing first with feeding the sound straight in, and a speech-only encoder with one trained on music and sound too. Then ask a transcript about music, about voices, or give a speech encoder a song.

lessons.title: Omni models: think, then talk
lessons.description: A homework helper in Lusaka watches a worksheet through the phone camera, hears "this one" as the student points, and explains aloud. A big Thinker writes what to say; a small Talker speaks it as it is written. Then order the tokens by type instead of time, make the Talker big, or wait for the whole answer before speaking.

lessons.title: Robots that see, read and act
lessons.description: A robot arm in an avocado packhouse in Murang'a is told: put the ripest avocado in the export crate. A vision-language-action model reads the camera and the words and outputs arm movements. Then train it on robot demos only, take away the safety layer, or use coarse action bins.

lessons.title: Documents: read the page
lessons.description: A clearing agent in Mombasa digitises cargo manifests: clean print, handwritten, skewed. Read them with an OCR pipeline or a vision model, and flag what is unsure.

lessons.title: ColPali: search the page itself
lessons.description: A farmer-support line in Arusha searches an illustrated extension manual for how to space maize and beans when intercropping. The answer is in a diagram. ColPali searches the page images patch by patch with MaxSim. Then search the text only, average the patches, or squeeze each page into one vector.

lessons.title: Multimodal RAG: ask across media
lessons.description: A travel desk in Stone Town looks for a quiet guesthouse by reviews, photos and sound clips. Each retriever scores on its own scale, so fuse by rank.

lessons.title: Computer-use agents: look, click, check
lessons.description: Capstone: an agent books a night coach from Nairobi to Kampala by looking at the booking site and acting one step at a time, until a person takes the last step.

lessons.title: Next word and temperature
lessons.description: A tiny language model offers its guesses for the next word as towers. Turn the temperature up and down, cut the short towers, and generate sentences. Then make it loop forever, or babble.

lessons.title: MDPs: states, actions, rewards
lessons.description: A boda-boda rider in Kampala carries medicine across a grid of streets past a flooded swamp edge. Change the discount and the rain, and watch the best route move.

lessons.title: Dynamic programming: sweep to the answer
lessons.description: A school in Accra plans fire-drill routes to the assembly point. Value iteration sweeps the floor plan until every room knows its distance out.

lessons.title: Monte Carlo: learn from whole trips
lessons.description: A mango trader leaves Techiman each morning for Wenchi or Kintampo, then stops or travels on. With no model of the markets, the trader learns which route pays by averaging what whole trips earned. Then never explore, learn from only ten trips, or keep averaging after a market falls.

lessons.title: Q-learning and SARSA: learn every step
lessons.description: A herder in the Simien Mountains moves goats from camp to the village along a ravine. The herder learns from every single step, Q-learning or SARSA style, while still exploring. Then stop after twenty days, or explore right on the edge with Q-learning.

lessons.title: DQN: a network that plays
lessons.description: A small phone game made in Abidjan: a basket catches falling mangoes. A deep Q-network learns to play from the screen alone, steadied by a replay memory, a frozen target network and Double DQN. Then take away replay, the target network or Double DQN, and watch learning wobble, collapse or overrate itself.

lessons.title: REINFORCE: push up what paid
lessons.description: A community radio station in Kano picks a time slot each day for a vaccination message. A policy learns straight from callers, with no value table in between.

lessons.title: Actor-critic: a player and a coach
lessons.description: A drone carries blood from a hub in Muhanga to a hill clinic. The actor decides how to fly; the critic estimates how good each waypoint is, and their difference scores each decision. Turn the λ dial between one-step and whole-flight estimates, then give it a poor critic, no critic, or no entropy bonus.

lessons.title: PPO: small safe steps
lessons.description: An SMS farm-advice line in Lilongwe tunes its replies from thumbs-up ratings. PPO reuses each batch several times, and the clip stops any one step going too far.

lessons.title: Reward models: learn what people prefer
lessons.description: A Swahili homework helper in Dar es Salaam is tuned from teachers' choices between pairs of answers. A reward model learns the score, then the tuner chases it.

lessons.title: Multi-agent RL: learning together
lessons.description: Two pirogues from Joal-Fadiouth choose where to set their nets each morning. Both at the rich ground is the best catch, but each one learning alone can get stuck.

lessons.title: Sim-to-real: from simulator to soil
lessons.description: A rover on a tea estate near Kericho must stop before the drain at the end of each row. Its braking was learned in a simulator, but real clay is slippery after rain. Train on one friction, a randomised range, a range far too wide, or let the rover sense slip. Then test it, dry or after rain.

lessons.title: Games: search, self-play, reasoning
lessons.description: A game studio in Kumasi trains an Oware player. Tree search looks ahead before each move, guided by a value estimate: the AlphaZero recipe, on an African board.

lessons.title: Tokenizers: words, letters or pieces
lessons.description: A Swahili-English school chatbot in Mombasa must cut a new sentence into tokens. Train four tokenizers on a tiny text and count the blocks each one makes.

lessons.title: Data pipelines: clean before you train
lessons.description: A lab in Nairobi builds a Swahili training set from a web crawl. Documents ride a conveyor through five gates, and each gate keeps less, and better.

lessons.title: Pre-training a mini GPT
lessons.description: A team in Kampala pre-trains a GPT-2-small-sized model on East African news. Build the stack, count its parameters exactly, and watch a good loss curve fall.

lessons.title: Distributed training: share the load
lessons.description: A university group in Cape Town plans a training run on rented 80 GB GPUs. See how memory fills for weights, gradients and state, and split it by the pipe.

lessons.title: Instruction tuning: from text to answers
lessons.description: A farmers' cooperative in Ibadan turns a base model, which only continues text, into an assistant that answers. Supervised fine-tuning does it, with a clean format.

lessons.title: RLHF: the full pipeline
lessons.description: A mobile-money help line in Accra tunes its assistant with human feedback: SFT, a reward model, then PPO. The proxy score climbs while the truth can part from it.

lessons.title: DPO: preferences without a reward model
lessons.description: A health hotline in Lagos tunes its assistant's answer to a worried parent. DPO learns straight from annotators' choices, with two models where RLHF runs four.

lessons.title: Constitutional AI: the model grades itself
lessons.description: A homework helper for students in Kumasi, Kisumu and Lusaka learns with almost no human labels: a written constitution, the model critiques itself, and it improves.

lessons.title: Evaluation: test it on your own task
lessons.description: A pharmacy chain with branches in Dar es Salaam, Kano and Kumasi must choose one of four models. A public benchmark, its own eval and an arena can disagree.

lessons.title: Quantization
lessons.description: Squeeze a model to fit on a phone. Each weight snaps to fewer allowed heights as the bits drop. Watch the memory fall and the errors grow, then let one giant weight ruin everything.

lessons.title: Inference: keep the GPU busy
lessons.description: A farm advice chat service for growers around Kigali, Arusha and Kumasi runs one model on one GPU. Writing each word means reading every weight from memory, so the trick is to write many people's words per read. Then serve one user at a time, wait for whole batches to finish, or give everyone a very long conversation.

lessons.title: The whole pipeline: from text to a served model
lessons.description: A team building a small assistant for Yoruba, Swahili and Amharic chains every stage of this track into one pipeline, each stage's hash feeding the next.

lessons.title: Open models: read the config
lessons.description: A lab in Kigali and a start-up in Cape Town choose an open model to run. Every one, from GPT-2 to DeepSeek-V3, is a config: read it, and see what it takes to run.

lessons.title: EAGLE-3: a smarter draft
lessons.description: A travel assistant in English and Swahili drafts words ahead with a tiny head that reads the big model's own states. The check keeps the answers exactly the same.

lessons.title: Differential attention: cancel the noise
lessons.description: A land office in Kampala asks who owns one plot, and the answer is one line in a long file. Two attention maps subtract, and the shared noise cancels out.

lessons.title: Native sparse attention: read the summaries first
lessons.description: A market office in Kumasi asks who signed the lease for stall 12. The lines sit far back in a long file, so score whole blocks first and read only the tall ones.

lessons.title: Multi-token prediction: two words ahead
lessons.description: A language model learns the next word at each position. DeepSeek-V3 adds a small module that also learns the word after, as training help and as a fast draft.

lessons.title: DualPipe: fill the gaps from both ends
lessons.description: A lab in Nairobi trains a mixture-of-experts model across a pipeline of GPUs. Blank time is waste, so overlap the traffic with the computing, in both directions.

lessons.title: DeepSeek-V3: keep the experts evenly busy
lessons.description: A lab in Addis Ababa trains a layer of 256 experts on eight machines, and every word picks eight. The step waits for the busiest machine, so balance them.

lessons.title: Jamba: mostly Mamba, a little attention
lessons.description: A legal aid clinic in Lusaka wants a model for long case files. Attention remembers every word at a cost; Mamba keeps a small state. Mix seven of one to one of the other.

lessons.title: Hogwild inference: many workers, one memory
lessons.description: A maths tutoring service in Accra asks a reasoning model about many cases. Hogwild runs workers at once that read each other's text, and finish sooner.

lessons.title: Speculative decoding: why the answer stays exact
lessons.description: Six words, two models. The draft guesses and the big model checks. See the one rule that keeps the output exactly the big model's.

lessons.title: Gradient checkpointing: recompute instead of store
lessons.description: A university lab in Kigali fine-tunes a 7-billion-parameter model on long documents. Keep every layer's values, or save memory and recompute them on the way back.

lessons.title: Prompt engineering: every rule removes a guess
lessons.description: A courier desk asks a model for handover notes. Stack the parts of the prompt, run 400 tries, and see which checks each part fixes.

lessons.title: Chain of thought: scratch paper, then a vote
lessons.description: A trader sells a third of 48 crates, then a quarter of the rest. Watch a model answer in one go, step by step, then many times with a vote.

lessons.title: Structured outputs: parse, check, send it back
lessons.description: A pharmacy wholesaler turns 200 order messages into records. Send each one through three gates and see what gets stored right, wrong or not at all.

lessons.title: Vector search: find the nearest without checking all
lessons.description: A helpline keeps 2,000 questions as vectors. Watch an HNSW index drop through its layers to find the five closest without checking them all.

lessons.title: Context engineering: what goes in the window
lessons.description: A support assistant fills its context window on every call. Choose what goes in and where, then watch what it gets right.

lessons.title: RAG: look it up first
lessons.description: A co-op's notes sit on a shelf. Ask a question and watch the right cards fly to the model before it answers. Switch the lookup off and it confidently makes things up.

lessons.title: Advanced RAG: fix the question, filter, widen
lessons.description: A university answers students from its handbook, with last year's edition beside it. Rewrite the question, filter the edition, and hand over whole sections.

lessons.title: LoRA: fine-tune a sliver, freeze the rest
lessons.description: A clinic in Kampala adapts an open model. LoRA freezes the weights and trains two thin matrices; watch the gap and memory towers.

lessons.title: Function calling
lessons.description: Watch a model ask for help. It writes a JSON slip, a gate checks it, the right tool runs, and the answer comes back. Then send it a broken slip and see why checking matters.

lessons.title: Regression tests: is the new prompt really better?
lessons.description: A bus-booking assistant in Abuja has a new prompt that scores higher on average. Check every category before the gate lets it ship.

lessons.title: Cost: cache, route, rate-limit
lessons.description: A helpline bot answers 10,000 questions a day. Add a rate limit, a cache and a router, and watch the bill and the wrong answers.

lessons.title: Guardrails: layers that catch what others miss
lessons.description: A bank assistant in Mombasa gets a thousand requests, some of them attacks. Stack checks before and after the model; each layer catches what others miss.

lessons.title: Production: retries, fallbacks, streaming
lessons.description: Results day at an exams helpline in Addis Ababa: traffic jumps fivefold, then the provider slows. Back off, fall back and stream to keep people answered.

lessons.title: MCP, stateless: every request carries its context
lessons.description: A clinic's booking assistant in Gaborone calls a calendar server forty times while one copy restarts. Sessions break; stateless requests don't.

lessons.title: Prompt caching: keep the start of the prompt the same
lessons.description: A college assistant in Zomba sends the same handbook, tools and examples every turn. Keep that start identical and the cache bills it at a tenth.

lessons.title: Agent graphs: state, checkpoints, a pause for people
lessons.description: A bus company's refund agent in Kigali, drawn as a graph with a checkpoint after every step, a pause for a person, and a server restart.

lessons.title: Agent frameworks: match the shape of the job
lessons.description: A lender in Lilongwe has six jobs for agents and five ways to build them. Find the style that fits each job, and what routing costs.

lessons.title: The tool interface: four steps across a glass wall
lessons.description: A model can only write words. Follow a slip across the glass to a host that does the real work, and back.

lessons.title: One tool, three providers: shapes and tool choice
lessons.description: A weather and alert assistant for Lake Victoria fishers declares its tools once and talks to three providers through one small translator.

lessons.title: Parallel tool calls: fan out, match by ID
lessons.description: A school trip planner in Kampala checks seats, weather in two towns and beds. Ask one at a time, all at once, or as they stream.

lessons.title: Structured output: three ways to get a clean order
lessons.description: Twenty order emails, three presses. See which failures each one can have, and what it pays to avoid them.

lessons.title: Tool design: names and descriptions pick the tool
lessons.description: A dairy co-op assistant in Eldoret has eight tools in confusing pairs. Watch 24 questions find their tool, and how much wording decides it.

lessons.title: MCP basics
lessons.description: See how an AI app plugs into files, calendars and weather through one standard socket. Envelopes of JSON travel down the pipes: hello, what can you do, please do this. Then break the handshake.

lessons.title: An MCP server: validate, route, label every reply
lessons.description: A notes server for health workers in Mzuzu answers twelve requests from three apps over stdio, each with exactly the reply the protocol asks for.

lessons.title: An MCP client: many servers, one tool list
lessons.description: A health office assistant in Mangochi connects to four MCP servers. Two share a tool name, one is old, one is slow, one restarts.

lessons.title: MCP over HTTP: one endpoint, checked headers, checked origin
lessons.description: A Nairobi pharmacy's laptop runs a local MCP server. Twelve HTTP requests arrive, some from places that should never reach it.

lessons.title: MCP resources and prompts: who chooses, and who may read
lessons.description: A school records server in Tamale offers tools, resources and prompts. Sort them by who chooses, then follow a teacher's eight requests.

lessons.title: MCP sampling: borrow the client's model, safely
lessons.description: A library server in Addis Ababa summarises a student's thesis folder with her own model, asking round by round through input_required.

lessons.title: Scope and asking the user: MCP elicitation
lessons.description: A legal-aid clinic in Kigali asks its notes server to delete an old draft lease: which folder may it touch, and which lease did she mean?

lessons.title: MCP tasks: long jobs with a handle
lessons.description: An exams office in Bulawayo builds a school's results report, a fifty-second job. The server hands back a task handle to poll.

lessons.title: MCP Apps: an interactive view, safely boxed
lessons.description: A parcel service in Lusaka shows a delivery timeline people can act on, boxed inside the chat app, with every action crossing a bridge.

lessons.title: Tool poisoning: pin what was approved
lessons.description: A Johannesburg newsroom approved its assistant's tools on Monday. On Tuesday four change. Pin what was approved, and quarantine the rest.

lessons.title: OAuth for MCP: right issuer, right audience
lessons.description: A bank's loan tools in Arusha accept only tokens made for them. Follow one morning of logins, a look-alike, a replayed token and a pass-through.

lessons.title: An MCP gateway: decide every request, fresh
lessons.description: A Kampala telecom puts one MCP gateway in front of billing, network and HR. It decides every request afresh and writes it down.

lessons.title: Auth in production: keys rotate, tokens get revoked, services fail
lessons.description: A health records server in Nakuru checks every token for a day: a key rotates, a phone is stolen, the token checker goes down.

lessons.title: A2A: hand a task to another company's agent
lessons.description: A Cape Town tour company's agent hands visa letters for twelve travellers to another firm's agent, which never shows its insides.

lessons.title: Tracing an agent: one trace from model to MCP server
lessons.description: A farm advisory agent in Mbale usually answers in three seconds, sometimes thirty. One trace shows every call, so the slow step can't hide.

lessons.title: A routing layer: aliases, fallbacks, budgets
lessons.description: A Lagos fintech gives four teams one model endpoint. Over one day a model retires, a provider fails and a batch job runs away.

lessons.title: Skills: know-how an agent loads when it needs it
lessons.description: A Harare mobile-money team packages its release check as a skill, then sorts the rest of its know-how into rules, hooks, tools and helpers.

lessons.title: Capstone: one request through the whole tool stack
lessons.description: A Dakar policy institute asks its assistant for a sourced brief. One request crosses a gateway, MCP, A2A, a task and an app view.

lessons.title: Skill discovery: show a catalog, load on demand
lessons.description: A Kinshasa logistics firm's coding agent has 200 skills. Show a short catalog, load one skill when a task matches, open only what it names.

lessons.title: Skill routing: eligible first, then best, or none
lessons.description: A Luanda software team's agent picks among four skills for twelve test requests: filter to the eligible, rank, and abstain when nothing fits.

lessons.title: Skill trust: the box matters more than the instructions
lessons.description: A Maputo team runs a code-review skill on strangers' pull requests. What the skill can reach matters more than what it says.

lessons.title: Skill evals: six layers before release
lessons.description: A Douala cloud team's diagnosis skill goes through six eval layers before release. Each layer catches what the others can't see.

lessons.title: Tool contracts: schemas, cursors, completions
lessons.description: A Bamako medical-supplies firm offers stock tools over MCP. Every exchange has a contract: schemas, page cursors, content and autocomplete.

lessons.title: Reliability: retries, cancels and reconnects without paying twice
lessons.description: A Blantyre cash-transfer programme pays households through an MCP tool. Replies get lost, cancels arrive late, two thousand tablets reconnect.

lessons.title: Registry admission: verify, pin, watch, roll back
lessons.description: A Windhoek payments team admits MCP servers from the registry. In one week: an impostor, a risky new version, drift and a withdrawn release.

lessons.title: Conformance: test the wire, not just the SDK
lessons.description: An Abidjan ID-verification team upgrades its MCP SDK. A corpus of recorded wire transcripts decides whether the new version ships.

lessons.title: Inside an object file: tables that point at tables
lessons.description: A Lagos bootcamp student opens the object file of their own program and finds every byte a home: header, code, symbols, names, relocations.

lessons.title: Disassembly: sweep or follow, then draw the graph
